paper.one_line_finding: With a GPT-4o partner instead of a human partner, AUT originality scored over all pair responses, GPT-4o's included (2,970 responses, 2,066 without GPT-4o's), was higher (Human-Human minus Human-AI B = -0.065, SE 0.007), did not differ once word count, fluency, and item were controlled (B = 0.010, SE 0.008, p = .201), and was lower for the participants' own responses (B = 0.029, SE 0.010, p = .005; Table 2, pp. 9-10).

arms.name: Human-AI

estimates.outcome: AUT originality-score variance, all collaborative responses
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Median-centered Levene test comparing the variance of CLAUS originality scores between partner conditions. CLAUS is a transformer model trained to match human originality ratings (PDF p. 5). This measures the spread of a quality score, rather than semantic similarity across people.

sources.quote: Levene’s test indicated a marginal significant difference in the variance of scores between the two conditions, F(1, 3036) = 3.72, p = .054.

estimates.notes: Higher outcome values mean a wider spread of originality scores, with no fixed direction for average creativity. The F statistic is unsigned. Neither arm variance nor arm mean is printed; Figure 3 is graphical only. Participant and response counts for this test are not printed and are not inferred from degrees of freedom. Levene testing treats responses as observations; no adjustment for repeated responses from participants is described. Human-AI pools human and AI contributions to the collaborative task; this is not a model-only arm. The prose p-value is retained; figure-only labels are not transcribed under extraction rule 1.

estimates.outcome: Short story diversity contribution, central-tendency comparison (Mann-Whitney)
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: Sentence-BERT paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2 embeddings. Within each condition, diversity is mean pairwise cosine dissimilarity among stories. Each story's diversity contribution is that condition's full diversity minus its diversity with the focal story omitted (PDF p. 7). The analysis compares these story-level contributions, not the two condition-level mean dissimilarities.

sources.locator: PDF p. 15, Creative Short Story Task, Diversity
sources.quote: diversity contribution scores between Human-AI (n = 72 pairs) and Human-Human (n = 68 pairs) conditions found no significant difference in their central tendencies (U = 2674, p = 0.347).

estimates.notes: The reported test is the Mann-Whitney U / Wilcoxon rank-sum test. Both story-diversity records concern the same score, contrast, and stories; they preserve the two different printed tests and must not be treated as independent evidence. PDF p. 15 reports Human-AI n = 72 pairs and Human-Human n = 68 pairs. These are collaborating dyads, not printed people counts for this analysis. Table 1 provides study-level people counts only; they are not substituted here. No total number of stories is printed, so n_units is null rather than a sum of the pair counts. The observation is one co-written story's contribution to its condition's diversity. The tests treat story contributions as observations without a correction for their dependence on the same condition-wide reference pool; se_basis is output. Higher contribution means the focal story increases its condition's dissimilarity more. Neither test supplies a signed treatment effect or a comparison of the two condition-level mean dissimilarities. No arm means, medians, SDs, SEs, intervals, or condition-level diversity scores are printed. Figure 7a supplies distributions only. SI 2 is not supplied. Preregistered_primary follows the paper's explicit identification of story diversity as a preregistered outcome domain (PDF p. 7), not a claim that either test was the study's unique primary analysis.
estimates.primary_override_reason: across_people, ai_vs_active. Two tests of the same contrast and score; neither allows a standardized effect. The Mann-Whitney test asks whether one arm's stories are more or less diverse, the across-people question; the Kolmogorov-Smirnov test detects any difference in the shape of the distribution.

estimates.outcome: Short story forward flow, condition coefficient
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Exploratory semantic distance between consecutive story sentences over the sentence sequence (PDF p. 15), following the forward-flow approach described on PDF pp. 6-7. The text describes human participants but does not explicitly state whether AI-written sentences are excluded.

stats.difference_is: The reported condition coefficient is Human-Human minus Human-AI (control minus treatment); sign retained as printed.

regression.model: Regression of adjacent-sentence semantic distance on condition, running sentence sequence, and their interaction. Human-AI reference is inferred from the description of a stable Human-AI trajectory and increasing Human-Human trajectory. The condition coefficient is at the sequence reference, not an average across positions. No DAT adjustment, participant random effects, or clustering are specified for this analysis on PDF p. 15.

sources.locator: PDF p. 15, Creative Short Story Task, exploratory forward-flow results
sources.quote: The main effect of condition was not significant (B = 0.002, SE = 0.016, t = 0.17, p = .90).

estimates.notes: Unit pair means two adjacent sentences, not a collaborating pair. The reported full-sample model condition coefficient is retained; the condition-by-sequence interaction is excluded as moderation. Higher semantic distance means greater within-story flexibility, not diversity across people. No person count, sentence-pair count, arm level, SD, or numerical interval is printed. Counts and coefficient degrees of freedom are not inferred from the overall model F test. The reported uncertainty is at the sentence-pair level; there is no described participant-level correction. The AUT-specific all-models DAT-adjustment statement on PDF p. 6 is not extended to this separately described exploratory story model; PDF p. 15 reports condition, running sequence, and their interaction, with no DAT or word-count adjustment stated. Its printed coefficient, SE, t statistic, and p-value are retained without recalculation.

estimates.outcome: Divergent Association Task score after collaboration, without the partner
estimates.question: after_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Each participant supplies 10 unrelated words. The DAT score is average pairwise cosine distance using GloVe trained on Common Crawl, multiplied by 100 (PDF p. 5). Higher scores indicate greater semantic divergence among that participant's own words.

sources.locator: PDF p. 9, AUT, Originality, descriptive paragraph
sources.quote: Humans in the paired group had an average DAT score of 75.4 while the humans in the AI group had a DAT score of 76.7.

estimates.notes: The DAT was completed individually after both collaborative tasks in the same session (PDF p. 4); therefore this is after_ai and immediate, even though the authors call DAT baseline verbal creativity and use it as a covariate. No arm-specific DAT count, SD, SE, test, or interval is printed. The comparison contains human DAT scores only. Flexibility follows the codebook rule for variety among one person's own responses and the reconciled screening form. This outcome was not explicitly designated as a primary post-assistance outcome.

open_items: The supplied PDF is the version-two preprint. The citation record identifies a later journal article, DOI 10.1016/j.chb.2026.109172, but that text is not supplied and differences remain unverified.

SI 1, SI 2, and supplementary deviations from the preregistration are referenced but absent from the supplied PDF; supplement-manifest.json lists no files. The registry at https://osf.io/tveaf was not read. Exact preregistered status of the AUT variance and forward-flow analyses and a unique primary outcome remain unconfirmed.

The AUT Methods state that all models control for DAT, administered after collaboration. The specific forward-flow Results describe linear regression without a complete formula or an explicit unadjusted exception. Both AUT forward-flow contrasts are therefore excluded under rule 5 pending clarification; they are listed in not_extracted.

The excluded all-response AUT forward-flow report contains inconsistent coefficient, SE, and t values and an interaction described as non-significant despite its printed p-value. No values are repaired.

No unadjusted originality effects or human-only AUT/story elaboration effects are printed. The reported mixed models include DAT measured after treatment; several additionally adjust for realized fluency or word count.

The paper does not print per-analysis people counts for the retained AUT, story-diversity, story-forward-flow, or DAT contrasts. Story diversity supplies dyad counts only. Counts are not reconstructed from degrees of freedom, pair counts, or study-level demographics.

Honesty-check exclusions are described without a count. The printed recruited total and Table 1 analyzed total agree, but the timing of exclusions and per-arm randomized people counts are not separately established. The matching/allocation mechanism is not fully described.

No SDs or uncertainty accompany the retained descriptive means. No arm variances accompany the Levene tests. No condition-level story-diversity scores or contribution arm means, medians, SDs, SEs, or intervals are printed.

The AUT descriptive fluency paragraph calls the overall figures total responses while reporting separate book and bottle means. The aggregation is unclear; all means are transcribed without doubling, summing, or averaging.

Story forward flow does not explicitly identify reference coding, sequence centering, whether AI sentences were excluded, or a correction for repeated sentence-pair observations. The printed condition coefficient is conditional on the sequence reference, not a reported marginal mean difference.

The story originality and word-count models do not fully specify whether each row covers the whole story or only a contributor's sentences, or whether GPT-4o receives a separate row. Those models are excluded for post-treatment adjustment.
The GPT-4o release year and participant country are not printed. The screening form lists no known shared sample with another paper.
